due_when.clears_when: Either the prop branch is reached unconditionally for a declared prop account (and that is shown by a test exercising all three states), or an operator decision records that the two bypass paths are acceptable and says why. ⚠️ A passing test of the ONE reachable state clears nothing -- that state already works.

origin.rerun: Read src/core/coordinator.py::_default_balance_fetcher in full and enumerate which branches reach src/prop/prop_balance.py::prop_sizing_balance.

what: src/core/coordinator.py::_default_balance_fetcher reaches prop_sizing_balance in only one of three states: cached_balance_usd is checked first and returns before the prop branch, and an account absent from live_balances takes branch 3 and never consults prop_balance at all. So the stale-balance sizing gate is weaker than prop_balance's own docstring implies.
why_it_matters: The gate is the reason it is considered safe for the prop status ask to go quiet while the book is flat -- the argument is 'sizing refuses on a stale balance, so nothing trades off a number nobody measured.' If the refusal is reachable in only one of three states, that argument is weaker than it reads, on a FUNDED account with an $87.34 cushion to an account-killer floor.
